title: Runtime Error Analysis & Stability Deep Dive
next_steps: Redwood to share relevant GPU kernel logs and cuDNN/CUDA versions (Priya)
Customer to reproduce failing job with debug flags and share S3 link (Liam)
Schedule 1-hour repro session on dedicated pool (Alex)
action_items: Priya Patel: collect and upload /var/log/nvidia and dmesg logs by 2025-02-03
Liam O'Neal: run repro with --debug-kv and attach KV cache snapshots by 2025-02-04

summary: Customer reported intermittent OOMs and CUDA driver timeouts when running production batch jobs on Redwood Dedicated. Deep dive covered batching, KV cache behavior, quantization profiles, retry semantics, driver versions, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed to repro on dedicated pool, collect kernel logs and KV snapshots, and schedule a follow-up repro session.
topics: KV cache eviction and prefix caching behavior
VPC + on-prem networking effects on timeouts
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Okay team, hi everyone, thanks for joining, um today we want to go deep on the stability issues you've been seeing — OOMs, CUDA timeouts, and retries. I'm Alex from Redwood, Priya our SE is here, and Jordan from SRE. Marta, Liam, Sara, thanks for making time.
[00:00:15] Marta Gomez: Yep thanks Alex, appreciate it. We've had a few jobs hit OOMs overnight and some CUDA watchdog timeouts, sporadic, we can't find a consistent repro.
[00:00:28] Priya Patel: Quick clarification, these are on Dedicated, correct? Reserved capacity GPUs, not the hosted API?
[00:00:33] Sara Liu: Correct, dedicated pool. We're running a pinned Llama-3-70B quantized model, int8-ish, using your quant profiles. Batch sizes vary; typical seq len around 16k tokens for some requests and that may be causing KV growth.
[00:00:50] Jordan Kim: We also saw some kernel-level NV driver resets in the logs, and dmesg showed NVRM: Xid 79 on a couple of nodes.
[00:00:58] Priya Patel: Okay that's the GPU soft ECC or driver timeout signals; Xid 79 typically correlates to a GPU page fault / context issue. We need the exact CUDA/cudnn and driver versions. Did you upgrade recently?
[00:01:10] Noah Park: We bumped CUDA from 12.1 to 12.2 last week as part of infra upgrades. Might be related.
[00:01:16] Alex Chen: Good to know. Two threads for today: one is runtime-level behavior (batching, KV cache, quantization) and the other is infra-level (drivers, watchdog, networking). We'll try to map where the failures live.
[00:01:30] Liam O'Neal: To give context: workload is a mix of streaming chat and long-completion pipelines. The long completions are where OOMs happen, usually after hundreds of autoregressive steps; sometimes it fails mid-regen with CUDA timeout.
[00:01:45] Priya Patel: That suggests KV cache accumulation per request — long histories mean larger KV caches. If prefix caching isn't used, continuous batching can amplify memory because multiple requests with long context may be coalesced into a single kernel invocation and peak memory gets high.
[00:02:00] Marta Gomez: Can you explain continuous batching? We thought batching was only per fixed window.
[00:02:05] Priya Patel: Sure — Redwood runtime has a continuous batching scheduler that accumulates tokens across concurrent requests and sends larger combined batches to improve throughput. It's great for cost but when you have variable sequence lengths, a batch can include one very long request plus many medium ones, and the peak memory equals sum of per-request KV sizes in that kernel call unless KV caching or model sharding reduces that.
[00:02:26] Sara Liu: We're using model sharding across 4 GPUs with ZeRO-like partitioning. Not sure if KV is sharded.
[00:02:33] Priya Patel: We shard weights but KV cache is options-based; in some configs KV is replicated per device to reduce cross-device comms which increases memory. Did you select replicated KV?
[00:02:44] Noah Park: I think the default for your Dedicated profile was replicated KV to reduce latency.
[00:02:49] Priya Patel: That explains the memory pressure. If KV is replicated across 4 GPUs, long contexts multiply memory footprint by 4. For 70B int8, with subword overhead, that can push you past device memory.
[00:03:02] Liam O'Neal: So what's the mitigation? Change to sharded KV?
[00:03:06] Priya Patel: Yes, switching to sharded KV reduces per-GPU KV memory at expense of cross-GPU comms. For very long contexts it's usually necessary. Alternatively we can cap batch window, enable prefix/persistent caching for repeated prefixes, or lower the per-request max tokens.
[00:03:22] Jordan Kim: Also we should look at quantization profile: some quantization schemes increase temporary activation buffers; certain kernels require FP16 intermediates. Which quant profile did you use?
[00:03:33] Sara Liu: We used Redwood's perf-recommended int8-matmul profile for 70B.
[00:03:37] Priya Patel: Some int8 matmul paths use additional temp buffers for dequantize-requantize and can blow up peak memory for long seqs. We can try alternative profile int8-lite which trades some speed for smaller temps.
[00:03:49] Marta Gomez: Hmm okay. About the CUDA timeouts, what causes those exactly?
[00:03:53] Priya Patel: The CUDA watchdog kicks if a kernel runs longer than the driver's timeout (often 2 seconds on some nodes). A huge combined batch or a pathological kernel (e.g., cross-device comm blocking) can trigger that. In addition, driver bugs in some 12.2 builds have caused unexpected Xid errors — we've seen regressions before.
[00:04:12] Liam O'Neal: So we should pin to 12.1?
[00:04:15] Priya Patel: Possibly. We'll check compatibility matrix. Jordan, can you paste the node driver and kernel versions?
[00:04:21] Jordan Kim: Yes I will attach later but we saw 525.xx drivers with CUDA 12.2 on a couple nodes.
[00:04:27] Alex Chen: Two parallel actions: collect driver/kernel logs and reproduce with a controlled workload on a dedicated repro pool. We'll provision with a pinned driver/CUDA combination.
[00:04:38] Noah Park: About retry semantics — our orchestrator retries idempotent requests but occasionally retries cause duplicated token generation because of partial progress state. How does Redwood handle mid-request retries?
[00:04:48] Priya Patel: Redwood's runtime has two retry modes: at the request router (idempotent retries) and at the backend (transient worker retries). For long streaming requests we checkpoint KV snapshots at safe boundaries; however, if a worker OOMs mid-seq the router may reissue the request from start which can cause duplicate tokens unless the client deduplicates. We can enable resumable streaming — that is, the runtime will persist a last-good KV snapshot in ephemeral storage and resume from that spot instead of restarting. There's a small latency/storage cost.
[00:05:13] Liam O'Neal: Is resumable streaming available in Dedicated?
[00:05:17] Priya Patel: Yes, it's an opt-in config for Dedicated. We'll show how to enable it.
[00:05:21] Sara Liu: One more: we saw timeouts in the client side consistent with transient network stalls in our VPC. Could VPC NAT/gateways cause long stalls that look like CUDA timeouts?
[00:05:31] Priya Patel: Not directly. CUDA timeouts are kernel-level. But network stalls can make the router wait for responses and increase time that a kernel stays resident with locks, exacerbating watchdog triggers in corner cases. Also if ephemeral NFS or KMS calls block it can starve GPU tasks.
[00:05:46] Marta Gomez: We are on cloud VPC with private subnets and some extra hops to our KMS. We saw occasional KMS latency spikes last week.
[00:05:53] Alex Chen: We'll include infra checklist: ensure KMS endpoints are highly available, avoid synchronous KMS calls in hot paths, and consider async key fetch.
[00:06:01] Priya Patel: Back to reproducing OOMs — best path: 1) create a repro job that sends a small number of requests but with long seq lengths to force large KV, 2) set continuous batching on to mimic production, 3) run with both replicated and sharded KV, and 4) capture per-GPU memory at high resolution and dmesg logs. We'll also enable verbose kernel-level logging in the runtime.
[00:06:25] Liam O'Neal: Sounds good. Can Redwood run this on a dedicated pool? Our infra team prefers you run it since the Dedicated pool is in your tenancy.
[00:06:32] Alex Chen: Yes we can provision a repro pool (4x A100 80GB) with controlled driver versions. Jordan will spin it up.
[00:06:38] Jordan Kim: I'll hand-provision a 4x80GB pool and pin drivers to 525.85 with CUDA 12.1 for the repro.
[00:06:45] Noah Park: Will that match our prod? Our prod currently uses 12.2.
[00:06:49] Alex Chen: We'll run two repros: one with 12.2 and one with 12.1 so we can isolate driver regressions.
[00:06:55] Priya Patel: Also we'll toggle KV mode and quant profiles. For quant, try int8-lite and fp16 for comparison.
[00:07:02] Sara Liu: Any quick config changes we can make now to reduce incidents?
[00:07:06] Priya Patel: Short-term: reduce batch window, enable sharded KV, or reduce max tokens allowed per request. Medium-term: switch quant profile to int8-lite and schedule a driver pin/rollback if we see driver correlation.
[00:07:18] Marta Gomez: About observability — what logs do you need? We can grant access to a bucket.
[00:07:23] Priya Patel: Need: per-GPU memory histograms (1s granularity), runtime verbose logs, NVidia driver logs (nvidia-smi -q -x), dmesg, and the worker stderr with stack traces. Also the exact request payloads (anonymized) to replicate tokenization.
[00:07:36] Liam O'Neal: We'll sanitize and drop into S3.
[00:07:39] Alex Chen: Great. Any questions on retry semantics?
[00:07:42] Noah Park: One: if a worker OOMs and router retries, can we enforce at-most-once?
[00:07:47] Priya Patel: At-most-once is hard for long-lived streaming; best is resumable streaming with a persisted KV snapshot and client-side dedupe tokens. We also support a transactional API for critical requests that writes outputs to durable storage atomically once complete.
[00:08:01] Marta Gomez: That helps. For compliance we need audit logs of retries and worker restarts.
[00:08:06] Alex Chen: Redwood Console exposes token-level traces and worker restarts. We'll add a retention policy note.
[00:08:11] Sara Liu: Any known bugs with 12.2 and Triton-like runtimes?
[00:08:15] Priya Patel: There were 12.2 driver regression reports in late 2024 causing Xid 79 in some cases for heavy GPU page table churn. We can test to confirm. Also Triton sometimes interacts badly with certain cuBLAS kernels; our runtime avoids those kernels for long seqs but quant paths can reintroduce them.
[00:08:36] Liam O'Neal: Ok we'll prepare artifacts. Timeline for next meeting?
[00:08:40] Alex Chen: Let's aim for early next week — repro session Tuesday 2025-02-04. We'll confirm after Jordan provisions.
[00:08:47] Marta Gomez: Works for us. Thanks.
[00:08:50] Priya Patel: I'll follow up with a checklist and the config snippets: how to switch KV sharded vs replicated, how to enable resumable streaming, and quant profile toggles.
[00:08:58] Alex Chen: Perfect. Thanks all.
[00:09:00] [call end - participants leaving]
